body_ar:
اشتملت سورة الإخلاص على إثبات وحدانية الله وصمديته، وأخذ منها العلماء الصفات الخمس السلبية في حق الله تعالى كما شرحها الشيخ حفظه الله تعالى.
انقسام الأشياء من حيث الغنى والحاجة إلى المحل والمخصص:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين. قال شيخنا حفظه الله في منظومته في الأسماء والصفات: [ وهو تعالى أحد فرد صمد ألحد من قال بخلقه اتحد ] بالنسبة للفظ (الفرد) فقد جاء في أحاديث ولم يرد في القرآن، وأما (الصمد) فإن صفة الصمدية مثبتة له، وهي الغنى المطلق عن خلقه، والغنى المطلق معناه: الاستغناء عن المحل والمخصص جميعاً. والأشياء فيما يتعلق بالحاجة والغنى عن المحل والمخصص أربعة أقسام: النوع الأول: ما يحتاج إلى المحل والمخصص معاً: وهو صفات المخلوقين، فهي محتاجة إلى المحل الذي تقوم به؛ لأنها صفة والصفة لا تقوم بنفسها بل تحتاج إلى محل تكون فيه، وذلك مثل البياض والسواد، والطول والقصر، فهذه لا بد لها من ذات تقوم بها، وتحتاج إلى المخصص. والمخصص المقصود به الخالق الذي يميز هذا المخلوق بست من اثنتي عشرة...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ comprises the affirmation of God's oneness and of His being the one eternally besought (ṣamad); and from it the scholars derived the five negating attributes in respect of God, exalted is He, as the Sheikh, may God preserve him, has explained them.

## The division of things in respect of independence of, and need for, a substrate and a determiner

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and God's blessing and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and his Companions all together. Our Sheikh, may God preserve him, said in his versification on the names and attributes: *[And He, exalted is He, is One, Single, eternally besought; whoever has said that He is united with His creation has deviated.]*

As for the word "al-Fard", the Single, it has come in reports and has not occurred in the Qur'an. As for "al-Ṣamad", the attribute of ṣamadiyyah is affirmed of Him, and it is absolute independence of His creation. Absolute independence means being in no need of either a substrate or a determiner.

Things, as regards need of and independence of a substrate and a determiner, fall into four divisions. The first kind: what needs both a substrate and a determiner together — and that is the attributes of created things. They need the substrate in which they subsist, because an attribute does not subsist by itself but needs a substrate to be in, as with whiteness and blackness, tallness and shortness: these must have an essence in which they subsist, and they need a determiner. By "the determiner" is meant the Creator, who marks off this created thing by six out of twelve …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
render as a complete text
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis in the middle of the first of the four divisions it announces, and in the middle of a technical formula that is left unexplained. Three of the four divisions are never given, and the five negating attributes named in the synopsis are never reached. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/esmawesivat-1.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed commentary
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, speaking about the lesson in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the lecturer's own words as transcribed, together with the quoted lines of the versified base text, which are his teacher's. Three voices in all, and the site must keep them apart.

flags.arabic: قال شيخنا حفظه الله في منظومته في الأسماء والصفات
flags.context: the formula introducing each quoted line of the versified base text in this series
options: read 'our Sheikh' as the author of the versification, the lecturer's own teacher
read it as Sheikh al-Dedew quoting his own verse
flags.note: Record 734 of this series settles the referent in a way the creed run (IDs 707-721) did not: it has 'قال شيخنا حفظه الله في منظومته في الأسماء والصفات' — 'OUR Sheikh, may God preserve him, said in his versification on the names and attributes'. The first-person plural possessive makes the author the lecturer's own teacher, living at the time of the lesson, and the base text a versification devoted specifically to the divine names and attributes. Elsewhere in the series the shorter 'قال الشيخ' and 'يقول الشيخ' are used for the same person. The author is nowhere named. Note that this is a different base text from the versified creed expounded in records 707-721, which record 719 identifies as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil.

flags.arabic: الغنى المطلق عن خلقه، والغنى المطلق معناه: الاستغناء عن المحل والمخصص جميعاً
options: absolute independence of His creation
unqualified independence of His creation
complete self-sufficiency from His creation
flags.note: The glossary homonym again, and the third occurrence of it in this slice after records 714 and 716. 'مطلق' is fixed in the glossary as 'unqualified', which is its legal-theory sense; here it is a creedal predicate meaning absolute, without any relativity. The second option would read as the technical opposite of 'muqayyad' and would make nonsense of a sentence about God's independence of all conditions. A reviewer should treat 'مطلق' as a standing hazard in this corpus: its sense is decided by whether the subject is a legal term or God.

flags.context: the technical pair on which the whole division turns
options: a substrate and a determiner
a locus and a specifier
a subject of inherence and an agent of particularisation
flags.note: Two technical terms of kalām, neither in the glossary, and the whole record is built on them. 'محل' is that in which an accident inheres and without which it cannot subsist — the text glosses it explicitly. 'مخصص' is that which determines a contingent thing to one of the alternatives open to it, and the text identifies it with the Creator. 'Substrate' and 'determiner' have been chosen as the least technical English that still holds the argument; the third option is more exact and unreadable. These renderings should be fixed corpus-wide before publication, since the pair will recur across the Names and Attributes series.

flags.arabic: يميز هذا المخلوق بست من اثنتي عشرة
flags.context: the last clause before the text breaks off
options: marks off this created thing by six out of twelve
distinguishes this created thing by six of the twelve
supply the twelve and the six from the kalām tradition
flags.note: The record breaks off in the middle of a formula that means nothing to a reader without the rest of the lesson. It belongs to the Ashʿari doctrine of determination, in which a contingent thing is determined to one member of each of a set of paired possibilities — existence or non-existence, one extent rather than another, one time, one place, one direction, one attribute — so that a determiner is required. Six of twelve would then be one from each of six pairs. That reconstruction has deliberately NOT been written into the translation, because the Sheikh does not give it in the served text and style guide section 6 forbids supplying reasoning he did not give. The English stops where the Arabic stops. This is the clearest case in the slice of a record that cannot be displayed as it stands.

flags.context: the second hemistich of the quoted verse
options: whoever has said that He is united with His creation has deviated
whoever holds that He is one with His creation has become a heretic
one who says He unites with His creation has gone astray
flags.note: A verdict on a named doctrinal position — the doctrine of union between God and creation — stated in half a line of verse and nowhere expounded in the served text. 'ألحد' is to turn aside from the right way; 'heretic' has been avoided because the English noun imports a trial and a verdict, where the Arabic verb states a deviation. The line is the base text's, not the lecturer's, and he does not comment on it in what survives. Style guide section 12: faithful in the file, and a decision before anything ships.

flags.arabic: لفظ (الفرد) فقد جاء في أحاديث ولم يرد في القرآن
flags.context: the lecturer's first remark on the verse
options: it has come in reports and has not occurred in the Qur'an
it is found in hadiths but not in the Qur'an
flags.note: A precise and deliberately limited claim about a divine name, and the English keeps it limited. He says the word occurs in reports and not in the Qur'an. He does not grade those reports, does not name them, and does not say whether the name may therefore be used; nothing of that has been supplied. The distinction bears on the much-discussed question of whether the divine names are confined to what is textually transmitted.

translator_notes: One of a run of fourteen records, IDs 734-747, the series 'The Names and Attributes', all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/esmawesivat-* series, numbered 1 to 14 in the same order as the IDs. None of the SEF aliases in this run carries a timestamp, so no upload date can be read from them.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The first record of the Names and Attributes series. It is also the densest in the slice: within four sentences of the opening formula it is deep in the technical vocabulary of kalām, with two untranslated technical terms and an unexplained numerical formula, and then it stops.

The English breaks the transcribed portion into three paragraphs where the source runs on, separating the quoted verse, the commentary on the two divine names, and the fourfold division. No word has been added or removed.

'صمد' is rendered 'the one eternally besought' with the Arabic retained, and the derived 'صمدية' as 'ṣamadiyyah', since the lecturer treats it as a named attribute. Neither is in the glossary and both should be added.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record. Style guide section 8 governs: everything predicated here is predicated of God.
